text:
sarah.k: Hey team — production started seeing intermittent 401s for users on Cloudflare Workers after we rolled the edge TS SDK 0.4.2 yesterday. Only affects the browser/edge bundle, server calls are fine. Happens under bursty traffic.
jun.support: Sorry you're hitting that — can you paste a minimal repro and a snippet of the failing request/headers? Is it consistent for the same user/session?
sarah.k: Not consistent. Attached quick snippet from worker client (we use the @redwood/inference edge bundle):
```js
// worker client code inside CF Worker script
import { createClient } from 'redwood-inference/edge';
const client = createClient({ apiKey: await getToken() });
await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-mini', prompt: 'hi' });
```
We call getToken() which refreshes tokens via an async call to our auth service. Failures show up as 401 from the API gateway.
lee.eng-runtime: Two suspicious vectors: preflight OPTIONS behavior in CF Workers and a race where async token refresh delays header attach. Can you paste the request log (server side) showing headers for the 401?
sarah.k: Server log for one 401:
```
[2026-03-10T14:12:03Z] request_id=abc123 method=POST path=/v1/generate status=401 headers={"content-type":"application/json","origin":"https://app.example.com"}
```
Notice Authorization is missing. Other successful requests show Authorization header present.
maria.qa: Repro steps we used locally: run worker via miniflare with 50 concurrent requests, sometimes 10-20% fail 401.
jun.support: That matches a race where the edge SDK wrapper awaits an async token promise after the fetch call is configured, causing the preflight/first attempt to go without Authorization. Cloudflare preflight/edge runtimes are strict and the gateway rejects missing auth on OPTIONS/POST flows. Two paths: workaround to ensure token is synchronous at callsite OR upgrade to the patched edge adapter.
lee.eng-runtime: There was a bug introduced in 0.4.2 in the edge adapter: token promise resolution was deferred after the request was scheduled which could lead to an OPTIONS or first fetch without Authorization header under concurrency. Fix landed in 0.4.3 — we now await token before building the fetch init and ensure header is set before any scheduling.
sarah.k: Oh nice. Is there a safe hotfix we can apply if we can't release 0.4.3 immediately?
jun.support: Workarounds: 1) Make getToken() synchronous for the first request (cache token client-side in worker global scope so the first concurrent callers don't trigger simultaneous refresh). 2) Attach a temporary static header from your server-side domain for critical routes. 3) Short term: throttle bursts (debounce calls) so token refresh finishes before next concurrent request. The proper fix is to upgrade to 0.4.3.
lee.eng-runtime: Also note: do NOT try to rely on cookies/credentials for bearer auth — preflight won't include cookies by default unless credentials: 'include', but that affects cookies not Authorization header. The real issue was the async ordering in the adapter.
sarah.k: We tried pinning back to 0.4.1 and the issue disappears. Good signal. We'll stage 0.4.3 rollout to production.
ops-bot: Deployed redwood/edge-adapter@0.4.3 to npm registry (published 2026-03-11T09:00:00Z).
maria.qa: Tested 0.4.3 on staging with miniflare and 1k concurrent bursts — no 401s observed across 10 runs.
sarah.k: Rolled 0.4.3 to prod canary — monitoring now, initial 15m looks green. Thanks for the quick triage. :tada:
jun.support: Glad it helped. Filing follow-up: add docs note about token refresh patterns in edge runtimes and recommended client caching patterns.
lee.eng-runtime: I'll open a small RFC to make the edge adapter tests include concurrent token-refresh scenarios so we don't regress.
sarah.k: 👍 thanks all
